arc: networkd: DeviceManager listens to all shill events always. Previously, arc-networkd would register/unregister shill handlers when ARC++ booted up or shut down, respectively. But in a multi-guest world, it needs to be aware of the host devices independent of guest lifecyles. And more specifically, for ARCVM it needs to be aware at VM boot time. *** This is a reland of https://crrev.com/c/1707790 *** BUG=b:133193765 TEST=units Change-Id: I6c95315b157e26ed450144909725b973f820623f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1828658 Tested-by: Garrick Evans <garrick@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Garrick Evans <garrick@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@google.com> Reviewed-by: Taoyu Li <taoyl@chromium.org>

arc: networkd: Move setup and teardown logic into ArcService. This patch refactors the setup/teardown, init/uninit and enable/disable code from ArcIpConfig into ArcService. Earlier attempts to break each logical unit into multicle CLs caused too many problems given the timing and interconencted nature of these pieces, due largely to the fact that the functionality was beig split across processes. Another key change in this patch is the gating of enable/disable on both sides of the veth pair being up. This is achieved by DeviceManager listening to rt netlink messages on the host and ArcService doing the same in the container's net namespace. Doing so, guarantees that once IPv6 route detection and address assignment runs, it can set up the datapath and configuration immediately. One caveat here is that the device keeps state that is currently specific to the ARC guest alone. This will have to be expanded, if necessary, to accomodate others. More functionality is moved into Datapath from ArcIpConfig. In order to add DeviceManager unit testing, a base class was added for mocking. ArcIpConfig unit test removed since it is no longer relevant. TODO: Add relevant tests to ArcSeviceTest *** This is a reland of https://crrev.com/c/1727633 but with the following fixes: (1) Devices are created once (as before) rather than repeated created and destroyed whenever the ArcService starts and stops. This is necessary to prevent shill from crashing when the virtual (wifi?) device is recreated (https://crbug.com/1008686). (2) The Android device is not added by default in DeviceManager but rather explicitly by the ArcService first starts. (3) ARC N boards not being enabled when the device manager detects the link is up. attestation/tpm_manager: Fix ODR violation in protobufs attestation/tpm_manager protos in system_api is used in both lib*.so and the actual binary/test runners. The end result is that when the actual binary/ test runners load the lib*.so, there'll be 2 copies of the protos. This is solved by not linking the protos into lib*.so. cros-disks: Force unmount network FUSE filesystems on EBUSY Unmounting filesystems will fail if it is being accessed. However, for drivefs and sshfs, there's no action a user can take to recover from such an error. Since these are FUSE filesystems, MNT_FORCE can be used to unmount the filesystem.
